intro.eyebrow: MARVI:  Managing Aquifer Recharge & Sustaining Groundwater Use through Village level intervention
intro.title: About MARVI
intro.lede: MARVI puts groundwater science in the hands of the people who depend on it—farmers, schools, researchers and communities working together for water that lasts!

heroImage.alt: Community members and researchers discussing a groundwater map

items.title: What is MARVI?
items.text: The aim is to improve irrigation-water security and rural livelihoods by making the invisible visible.

photo.alt: Villagers and researchers discussing groundwater together

items.title: Why groundwater?
items.text: Rain moves through soil and rock into an aquifer. Wells reveal only a small window into a connected underground system.

items.title: The MARVI journey
items.text: How can a village understand an invisible shared resource—and decide its future together?

photo.alt: The MARVI team, researchers and village volunteers

items.title: Where MARVI works
items.text: MARVI acknowledges the women and men of the Dharta and Meghraj watersheds whose observations, experience and leadership shaped the project.

items.title: People & Partners
items.text: Researchers, practitioners and village volunteers in India and Australia working as one team.

photo.alt: Researchers and partners from India and Australia at a MARVI workshop
